projects.title: mtld3d
projects.game: Windows Direct3D 9 applications and games through Wine (multi-title)
projects.platform: Direct3D 9 → Metal through Wine on macOS 15/26 (Apple silicon) or macOS 15 (Intel CI); requires a Wine build based on CrossOver 26, with CrossOver 27 arm64 Wine tested locally
projects.status: Active; v0.13.0 was released 2026-10-13. The maintainer's tested list includes World of Warcraft 1.12/3.3.5a, Half-Life 2, Team Fortress 2, Grand Theft Auto IV, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, Age of Empires II: HD Edition, League of Legends 4.20, and several Need for Speed titles. Those are title-specific tests, not a universal compatibility guarantee.
projects.summary: Open-source Direct3D 9 implementation for Wine on macOS. Its Wine DLL implements the D3D9-facing API, translates shader models 1–3 from DXSO to Metal Shading Language, and submits rendering through Metal. A 64-bit Wine prefix is required; 32-bit games use WoW64. The project documents its tested games and unsupported D3D9 behavior separately.
projects.strategy: Direct3D 9 API implementation and shader/command translation to Metal inside Wine
projects.source_available: Public source repository under the zlib license; Wine is a separate runtime dependency
projects.subtype: macOS Direct3D 9 graphics API layer for Wine

projects.title: Hangover
projects.game: Windows x86/x86-64 applications on ARM64 Linux (multi-title)
projects.platform: Windows x86-32/x86-64 applications → ARM64 Linux using ARM64 Wine; ARM32 Windows applications can also run on x86-64 Linux
projects.status: Active; hangover-11.16 was released 2026-08-30. The upstream README lists Debian 11–13 and Ubuntu 20.04–25.10 packages. The project documents app-level x86 translation through FEX and/or Box64; its README does not claim a general game compatibility rate.
projects.summary: Wine-based Windows compatibility layer for ARM64 Linux. Hangover keeps Wine native on ARM64 and uses per-application emulator DLLs to translate x86/x86-64 instructions with FEX and/or Box64, rather than emulating an entire machine or running an x86 Wine installation. Wine handles Windows APIs; optional graphics components such as DXVK remain separate and require a suitable Vulkan driver.
projects.strategy: Native ARM64 Wine API compatibility plus per-process x86/x86-64 ISA translation through FEX or Box64
projects.source_available: Public source repository under LGPL-2.1; submodules and bundled components retain their own licenses

projects.title: x87sidecar
projects.game: x86 programs with x87 workloads, including older Windows games under Wine (multi-title)
projects.platform: x86/x86-64 macOS or Windows applications through Wine → Apple silicon macOS ARM64 using Rosetta 2; Windows integration requires the maintainer's patched Wine handshake
projects.status: Active; v1.9.0 was released 2026-10-13. The project says CI runs on macOS 26 and that it also runs on macOS 27; its probe checks whether the installed Rosetta runtime is supported. It accelerates only documented x87 instruction ranges, while stock Rosetta handles other instructions.
projects.summary: A specialist ISA-translation extension for Apple Rosetta 2 on Apple silicon, not a general x86 emulator or Windows API layer. It hooks Rosetta's x86 translator and emits AArch64 code for selected x87 floating-point blocks; unhandled instructions fall through to stock Rosetta. For Windows programs, the project requires a patched Wine build that performs its cooperative sidecar handshake. Its README documents arithmetic-precision limits and notes that its large speedup figures come from microbenchmarks, not whole-game performance.
projects.strategy: Rosetta-integrated JIT translation of selected x87 instructions to AArch64
projects.source_available: Public MIT-licensed source; requires Apple's proprietary Rosetta 2, and Wine support uses a separately published patched Wine build
projects.subtype: x87 ISA translation/JIT extension for Rosetta 2

projects.title: Ferrum
projects.game: Windows x86/x86-64 games on Apple silicon (multi-title; no end-to-end game is yet claimed)
projects.platform: Planned Windows x86/x86-64 → Apple silicon macOS ARM64 stack using FEX, Wine, DXVK/vkd3d-proton, and MoltenVK/Metal; the project says it is designed not to depend on Rosetta
projects.status: In development; no public Ferrum release or source is available as of 2026-10-15. The maintainer reports a D3D11 device and rendered frame reaching a macOS window, but explicitly says no full game has been driven end to end. The published architecture and delivery policy are not claims that the complete stack has shipped.
projects.summary: A proprietary compatibility engine in development for Windows games on Apple silicon. Its published design uses native ARM64 host components, FEX for x86/x86-64 instruction translation, Wine for Windows APIs, Direct3D-to-Vulkan layers, and MoltenVK to reach Metal. The implementation is private; the public GitHub repository is documentation only, and the maintainer does not claim a playable full-game result yet.
projects.strategy: Planned native ARM64 compatibility stack: FEX ISA translation, Wine API compatibility, Direct3D-to-Vulkan, and Vulkan-to-Metal
projects.source_available: Proprietary and closed source; public GitHub repository contains documentation only and no public Ferrum release was listed
projects.subtype: Apple silicon Windows-game compatibility engine (in development)
